reasons: Lake record verifies Carpenter v. United States as a U.S. Supreme Court case decided in 2018.
Lake official/display citation is 585 U.S. 296, matching the page citation.

defect.evidence_quote: ## Issue Whether police may, without a warrant, search the digital contents of a cell phone seized from an individual incident to arrest. ## Rule A warrant is generally required.
defect.problem: The core Riley rule is partly supported, but the black-letter assertion as framed is not fully verifiable from disclosed evidence: the exact quoted sentence is absent from the Riley pinpoint quote, pin-403 is marked quote_fidelity mismatch/slip-only, the physical-aspects clause lacks disclosed text support, and the black-letter rule lacks two affirmative approvals.
defect.proposed_fix: Keep only the disclosed-supported paraphrase that a warrant is generally required to search digital contents seized incident to arrest, or add full Riley text/matched pinpoints for pages 387 and 403 plus a second affirmative authority before presenting it as black-letter.

reasons: No text/Riley file is disclosed, so verbatim quote fidelity can only be checked against lake pinpoints.
Riley pin-403 does not contain the quoted sentence beginning "Our answer to the question" and is recorded as quote_fidelity mismatch with pinpoint_status slip-only.
The disclosed Riley material supports only the narrower rule that a warrant is generally required for digital contents seized incident to arrest.
The assertion also says officers may inspect physical aspects and may search data under separate exceptions, but those clauses are not verified by the disclosed Riley pinpoint quote.
As a black-letter callout, it does not show the required two affirmative approvals from disclosed authorities.
residual_risks: Full Riley opinion text might verify the exact quote and physical-inspection clause, but it is not present in the disclosed evidence.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Split the rule into a verified Riley paraphrase and separate, pinned support for physical inspection, exceptions, and the quoted warrant sentence.
